title: Establish PRD triage decision ropes and legal acknowledgement path for scope shifts
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Recent PRD scope changes have led to ambiguous ownership and delayed signoffs across Engineering, Design, and Legal. This ambiguity increases rework, blocks downstream rollout (Dedicated/Private), and surfaces last-minute compliance questions. Goal: Define a lightweight, repeatable 'triage decision rope' — a documented path and SLA for how scope changes, clarifying questions, and acceptance criteria are raised, routed, and acknowledged by Design and Legal before engineering starts major work. Deliverables: 1) A triage decision flow (who decides, by when) for small/medium/large scope changes. 2) A one-page Legal acknowledgement template (data classification, PII considerations, contract risk flags). 3) A Design acceptance checklist (UX guardrails, accessibility, localization impact). 4) A signoff SLA matrix and rollback triggers. 5) A Playbook page (Confluence) + a short README used in PRD templates and gating steps in the Console rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Flow doc (Confluence) published and linked from PRD template
Legal acknowledgement template accepted by Legal lead (signature comment in Confluence)
Design checklist adopted by Product-Design as the default for PRDs (verified by Design lead)
SLA matrix defined: minor = 3 business days, medium = 7 business days, major = 14 business days
At least two cross-team mock PRDs run through the flow with retros and captured issues
Rollout plan includes a rollback trigger definition and owner for each risk tier
